title: Jensen Huang on AI alarmism: jobs, safety as engineering, open models, and the five-layer cake
summary: Jensen argues AI is a revolution best understood as software and engineering, not myth. He separates a job's purpose from its tasks, says safety is part of accelerating AI, and backs open models and diffusion across every industry. He also rejects doomer narratives as harmful.

principles.text: Every job has a purpose and tasks. AI automates tasks, not the purpose, so jobs change rather than vanish.
principles.quote: for everybody's job, there's the purpose of the job and then there's the task you do as the job.

principles.text: Human ambition is the missing input in job-loss forecasts; he expects net job creation and new industries.
principles.quote: I believe the power of ambition is the greatest force in fact and is missing in everybody's calculation

principles.text: Treat AI as an engineering problem: root-cause failures, fix the process. If you can't control it, don't ship it.
principles.quote: if they believe they're out of control, then the right answer is don't ship products until they're in control.

principles.text: Safety, alignment and evaluation are part of accelerating the technology, not a brake on it.
principles.quote: AI needs to accelerate to be safe.

principles.text: Alarmism isn't a social good. Be scientific and evidence-based, because scaring people harms society.
principles.quote: Don't think for a second just because you're an alarmist that you're doing a social good.

principles.text: Responsible optimist: carry the worries yourself and give others the optimism. The hard problems are the builder's.
principles.quote: it turns out that's not society's problem. That's my problem.
